jobs.excerpt: Wanted: Colonist DevOps Engineer Working Hours: We work asynchronously and value outcomes over hours Location: Fully Remote Compensation: Paid in USD.
jobs.description:
Wanted: Colonist DevOps Engineer

Working Hours: We work asynchronously and value outcomes over hours

Location: Fully Remote

Compensation: Paid in USD. Negotiable based on experience and location

About Colonist

We're building the biggest digital board game platform on the internet. Players start 250k games every day. Last year: 60M games, 3,037 years of play. We're a fully remote, asynchronous team spread across multiple continents, focused on crafting extremely polished digital board games that people truly love.

About The Role

Most apps scale by splitting users apart. We can't. Players share one live game state. Every lag spike is felt mid-game. One viral video can 10x our traffic overnight. Your job: absorb 50k CCU without dropping a single game.

You will own the infrastructure behind every game session: clusters, deploys, databases, the edge, and the path from merge to production. You will make our infra knowledge shared, so no system depends on one person.

What You'll Do

  • Own the stack behind every game: game, matchmaking and lobby servers on Kubernetes

  • Manage cluster and cloud resources as code in Terraform

  • Scale servers up and down with live traffic. Pay for players, not idle machines</

jobs.title: Architecture Operations Specialists: Structured Data for Post-Training Evaluatio
jobs.excerpt: What We're ResearchingWe're running a paid study on data structuring practices within architecture firms.
jobs.description:
What We're Researching

We're running a paid study on data structuring practices within architecture firms. Transforming messy operational data into clean evaluations and structured formats is critical for post-training workflows. Help us evaluate the current methodologies and challenges teams face when organizing this specialized architectural data.

How It Works

You will participate in a remote video interview to discuss how your firm handles operational data. We will ask you to walk us through the end-to-end process of turning unstructured architectural data into usable evaluations. You will be shown a few hypothetical data transformation scenarios and asked to provide feedback on potential workflow improvements. We will also ask you to describe the specific tools and practices your team relies on for post-training data management.

Who This Is For

We are looking for operations specialists, data managers, and technical architects who handle operational data within architecture firms. We welcome data operations leads, BIM managers, and internal workflow specialists with direct experience in post-training evaluations. If you regularly wrangle messy firm data into structured formats, this study is a great fit.

What You'll Do

  • Discuss how your architecture firm transforms messy operational data into structured evaluations.

  • Walk us through your day-to-day data management and post-training workflows.
